The properties
<MATH_0001>``<MATH_0002> is locally quasi-finite''
and
<MATH_0003>``<MATH_0004> is quasi-finite''
are fpqc local on the base.

We have already seen that ``quasi-compact'' is fpqc local on the base, see
Lemma <REF_0001>. Hence it is enough
to prove the lemma for ``locally quasi-finite''. We will use
Lemma <REF_0002>
to prove this. Assumptions (1) and (2) of that lemma follow from
Morphisms of Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0003>.
Let <MATH_0001> be a surjective flat morphism of affine schemes over <MATH_0002>.
Let <MATH_0003> be a morphism of algebraic spaces, and assume
that the base change <MATH_0004> is locally quasi-finite.
We have to show that <MATH_0005> is locally quasi-finite. Let <MATH_0006> be a scheme
and let <MATH_0007> be surjective and <ACCENT_0001>tale. By
Morphisms of Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0004>
again, it is enough to show that <MATH_0008> is locally quasi-finite.
Since <MATH_0009> is locally quasi-finite, and since <MATH_0010> is a
scheme <ACCENT_0002>tale over <MATH_0011> we conclude (by the same lemma again) that
<MATH_0012> is locally quasi-finite.
As <MATH_0013> is an fpqc covering we conclude that
<MATH_0014> is locally quasi-finite by
Descent, Lemma <REF_0005>
as desired.
